result.summary: Confirmed the rework item is genuinely fixed. `grep` of lib/letflow/definitions.ex shows the CASE SQL literal 'CASE WHEN lower(?) = lower(?) THEN 3.0 WHEN ? ILIKE ? THEN 2.0 ELSE 1.0 END' now appears exactly once, at line 719, as the `@rank_case_sql` module attribute. Both call sites (`select_with_rank/3` at line 726 and `order_by_rank/3` at line 741) reference it via `fragment(@rank_case_sql, d.name, ^search_query, d.name, ^pattern)` with identical, unchanged argument order/values -- no drift between them. The surrounding comment (lines 702-718) correctly explains why a module attribute works here (inlined as a literal before Ecto's fragment/1 SQL-injection macro guard runs) versus why a helper-function call would not. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` passes clean after touching the file. This is a minimal, idiomatic use of a module attribute for a compile-time-constant string shared between two private functions -- not scope creep, and it touches no supervision or process code (this is Ecto query-building logic in definitions.ex, not process_instance.ex or the supervision tree), so no new idiom/scope/supervision issue was introduced.
